{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Jq6eJjR5RthoShcD7anmkt","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Sargas Pharmaceutical Adherence and Compliance International — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: http://www.spacinternational.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Sargas Pharmaceutical Adherence and Compliance (SPAC) International is a small, privately held digital health company based in Bakersfield, CA, founded by Gitesh (Git) Patel. The company originally focused on helping cancer patients maintain medication adherence despite side effects, then expanded into chronic care management when CMS approved CCM reimbursement (CPT 99490 etc.) in 2015. SPAC International also operates under the brand \"hru2day\" (as in \"how are you today\").\n     9→\n    10→The company is a niche vendor focused exclusively on chronic care management, remote patient monitoring, and medication therapy monitoring — it is **not** a full EHR. It serves physician practices, hospitals, health plans, ACOs, FQHCs, and home health agencies, primarily for Medicare patients with chronic conditions. According to the hru2day website, the platform serves 20,000+ patients across 200+ practices with 200,000+ recorded interactions. The company operates a 24/7 clinical call center staffed by trained professionals who provide care coordination on behalf of contracting physician practices. The business model involves contracting with physician practices and sharing Medicare CCM/PCM/RPM reimbursement revenue.\n    11→\n    12→The company engaged PYA (an advisory firm) to verify compliance with Medicare billing rules for relevant CPT codes. It has no apparent acquisition history, parent company, or rebranding beyond the addition of the \"hru2day\" consumer-facing brand.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: Sargas International's Chronic Care Management Cloud dba hru2day\n    15→\n    16→CHPL ID: 10702\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→The Chronic Care Management Cloud (branded hru2day) is a cloud-based platform for managing chronic care patients, primarily under Medicare CCM, PCM (Principal Care Management), and RPM (Remote Patient Monitoring) programs. It achieved ONC HIT Modular EHR certification (version 21.9, certified October 14, 2021) — notably as a **modular** certification, not a complete EHR. The product was previously certified under the 2014 Edition as well (version 14.1).\n    21→\n    22→The certified criteria are relatively focused:\n    23→- **(a)(1)–(a)(3), (a)(5)**: CPOE for medications, labs, diagnostic imaging; demographics; problem list\n    24→- **(b)(10)**: EHI export\n    25→- **(d) criteria**: Security, authentication, audit logging\n    26→- **(e)(2)**: Clinical information reconciliation (not patient portal VDT)\n    27→- **(g)(10)**: Standardized FHIR API\n    28→- **(g)(3)–(g)(5)**: Safety-enhanced design, quality management, accessibility\n    29→\n    30→Notably absent from certification: e-prescribing, transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), patient portal view/download/transmit (e)(1), and all public health reporting (f) criteria. This aligns with the product being a care management platform rather than a point-of-care clinical EHR.\n    31→\n    32→### Users & Market\n    33→\n    34→**Primary users**: Care coordinators and clinical staff at the 24/7 call center, physician practice staff, and physicians who review care plans and patient data. Patients interact through mobile apps and a patient portal.\n    35→\n    36→**Clinical settings**: Ambulatory physician practices (often small to mid-size), ACOs, FQHCs, home health agencies, and hospitals — all serving Medicare populations with chronic conditions.\n    37→\n    38→**Scale**: 200+ practices, 20,000+ patients, 200,000+ interactions (per the hru2day website). This is a small vendor by any measure.\n    39→\n    40→**Go-to-market**: The company contracts directly with physician practices. SPAC's call center staff perform the actual CCM services (phone calls, care plan updates, medication monitoring) on behalf of the practice, and the practice bills Medicare. This is a managed-service model — SPAC is both the technology vendor and the care management service provider.\n    41→\n    42→### Modules & Functionality\n    43→\n    44→The platform consists of several interconnected components described across vendor materials:\n    45→\n    46→**Physician Portal**: Allows physicians to review patient care plans, medication lists, health data, and care coordination activity performed by the call center staff. Provides a centralized view of patient information.\n    47→\n    48→**Patient Portal / Mobile App**: Gives patients access to their care team, secure messaging, medication reminders, and the ability to report symptoms and side effects. The Drug Adherence® mobile app provides medication reminders and side effect reporting.\n    49→\n    50→**Pharmacy Portal**: Enables real-time health information exchange with pharmacies. Details on specific pharmacy functionality are limited.\n    51→\n    52→**Chronic Care Management (CCM)**: Core module supporting CMS CCM requirements — creation and maintenance of patient-centered care plans addressing physical, mental, cognitive, psychosocial, functional, and environmental needs. Includes structured recording of demographics, problems, medications, and allergies. Supports at least 20 minutes/month of care management per patient.\n    53→\n    54→**Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)**: Captures physiological data from FDA-approved home monitoring devices (glucose monitors, blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, weight scales, heart rate monitors). Data is transmitted in real-time to the care team.\n    55→\n    56→**Medication Therapy Monitoring (MTM) / Drug Adherence**: Tracks medication adherence, provides reminders, monitors for side effects, and checks for drug interactions. Originally developed for oncology medication adherence — this was the company's founding use case.\n    57→\n    58→**Principal Care Management (PCM)**: Extended care management for high-risk patients requiring 30+ minutes of monthly care coordination.\n    59→\n    60→**Care Transitions Management**: Coordination for patients transitioning between settings — includes emergency department follow-up and hospital discharge coordination.\n    61→\n    62→**24/7 Clinical Call Center**: While not a software module per se, this is integral to how the platform operates. Trained clinical staff provide the care management services, logging all interactions in the system.\n    63→\n    64→**AI/ML capabilities**: The vendor claims to use artificial intelligence and machine learning for identifying health risks and enabling preventive interventions, though specific details are not provided.\n    65→\n    66→### Data & Content\n    67→\n    68→Based on vendor materials, the platform manages the following data:\n    69→\n    70→**Clinical data explicitly described**:\n    71→- Patient demographics\n    72→- Problem lists (chronic conditions)\n    73→- Medication lists and medication allergies\n    74→- Care plans (comprehensive, addressing physical, mental, cognitive, psychosocial, functional, and environmental domains)\n    75→- Physiological monitoring data: glucose, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, weight (from RPM devices)\n    76→- Medication adherence records and side effect reports\n    77→- Clinical summaries\n    78→\n    79→**Interaction and workflow data**:\n    80→- Care coordination logs (documenting the 20+ minutes/month of CCM services)\n    81→- Call center interaction records (200,000+ interactions logged)\n    82→- Secure messages between patients, care teams, and providers\n    83→- Referral and care transition records\n    84→- Patient consent records (required for CCM billing)\n    85→\n    86→**Billing-relevant data**:\n    87→- Time tracking for CCM/PCM/RPM services (linked to CPT codes 99439, 99437, 99487, 99489, 99490, 99491 for CCM; 99424-99427 for PCM)\n    88→- Service documentation supporting Medicare reimbursement\n    89→\n    90→**What's unclear or likely absent**:\n    91→- The website does not describe clinical notes/encounter documentation in the traditional EHR sense (progress notes, H&P, etc.)\n    92→- No mention of lab result storage (though CPOE for labs is certified, suggesting orders can be placed)\n    93→- No mention of diagnostic imaging results\n    94→- No mention of immunization records\n    95→- No mention of scheduling/appointment management\n    96→- No mention of billing/claims processing beyond CCM/PCM/RPM time tracking — the actual Medicare billing appears to be done by the physician practice, not through this system\n    97→- No mention of document management or scanned records\n    98→\n    99→The product's data footprint is specialized: it's deep on care plans, medication monitoring, physiological data from RPM devices, and care coordination activity logs, but narrow compared to a full EHR. It does not appear to be the primary clinical documentation system for any practice — rather, it supplements the practice's existing EHR with CCM/RPM/MTM-specific capabilities.\n   100→\n   101→---\n   102→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You CAN and SHOULD provide analysis of malware, what it is doing. But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"75646119-9221-4382-b7e5-5d3f8f25469b","uuid":"09ff704b-55f0-4d28-b829-ff245a5f4e06","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/sargas-pharmaceutical-adherence-and-compliance-international/product-research.md","content":"# Sargas Pharmaceutical Adherence and Compliance International — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-15\nDeveloper website: http://www.spacinternational.com\n\n## Overview\n\nSargas Pharmaceutical Adherence and Compliance (SPAC) International is a small, privately held digital health company based in Bakersfield, CA, founded by Gitesh (Git) Patel. The company originally focused on helping cancer patients maintain medication adherence despite side effects, then expanded into chronic care management when CMS approved CCM reimbursement (CPT 99490 etc.) in 2015. SPAC International also operates under the brand \"hru2day\" (as in \"how are you today\").\n\nThe company is a niche vendor focused exclusively on chronic care management, remote patient monitoring, and medication therapy monitoring — it is **not** a full EHR. It serves physician practices, hospitals, health plans, ACOs, FQHCs, and home health agencies, primarily for Medicare patients with chronic conditions. According to the hru2day website, the platform serves 20,000+ patients across 200+ practices with 200,000+ recorded interactions. The company operates a 24/7 clinical call center staffed by trained professionals who provide care coordination on behalf of contracting physician practices. The business model involves contracting with physician practices and sharing Medicare CCM/PCM/RPM reimbursement revenue.\n\nThe company engaged PYA (an advisory firm) to verify compliance with Medicare billing rules for relevant CPT codes. It has no apparent acquisition history, parent company, or rebranding beyond the addition of the \"hru2day\" consumer-facing brand.\n\n## Product: Sargas International's Chronic Care Management Cloud dba hru2day\n\nCHPL ID: 10702\n\n### What It Is\n\nThe Chronic Care Management Cloud (branded hru2day) is a cloud-based platform for managing chronic care patients, primarily under Medicare CCM, PCM (Principal Care Management), and RPM (Remote Patient Monitoring) programs. It achieved ONC HIT Modular EHR certification (version 21.9, certified October 14, 2021) — notably as a **modular** certification, not a complete EHR. The product was previously certified under the 2014 Edition as well (version 14.1).\n\nThe certified criteria are relatively focused:\n- **(a)(1)–(a)(3), (a)(5)**: CPOE for medications, labs, diagnostic imaging; demographics; problem list\n- **(b)(10)**: EHI export\n- **(d) criteria**: Security, authentication, audit logging\n- **(e)(2)**: Clinical information reconciliation (not patient portal VDT)\n- **(g)(10)**: Standardized FHIR API\n- **(g)(3)–(g)(5)**: Safety-enhanced design, quality management, accessibility\n\nNotably absent from certification: e-prescribing, transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), patient portal view/download/transmit (e)(1), and all public health reporting (f) criteria. This aligns with the product being a care management platform rather than a point-of-care clinical EHR.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Primary users**: Care coordinators and clinical staff at the 24/7 call center, physician practice staff, and physicians who review care plans and patient data. Patients interact through mobile apps and a patient portal.\n\n**Clinical settings**: Ambulatory physician practices (often small to mid-size), ACOs, FQHCs, home health agencies, and hospitals — all serving Medicare populations with chronic conditions.\n\n**Scale**: 200+ practices, 20,000+ patients, 200,000+ interactions (per the hru2day website). This is a small vendor by any measure.\n\n**Go-to-market**: The company contracts directly with physician practices. SPAC's call center staff perform the actual CCM services (phone calls, care plan updates, medication monitoring) on behalf of the practice, and the practice bills Medicare. This is a managed-service model — SPAC is both the technology vendor and the care management service provider.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nThe platform consists of several interconnected components described across vendor materials:\n\n**Physician Portal**: Allows physicians to review patient care plans, medication lists, health data, and care coordination activity performed by the call center staff. Provides a centralized view of patient information.\n\n**Patient Portal / Mobile App**: Gives patients access to their care team, secure messaging, medication reminders, and the ability to report symptoms and side effects. The Drug Adherence® mobile app provides medication reminders and side effect reporting.\n\n**Pharmacy Portal**: Enables real-time health information exchange with pharmacies. Details on specific pharmacy functionality are limited.\n\n**Chronic Care Management (CCM)**: Core module supporting CMS CCM requirements — creation and maintenance of patient-centered care plans addressing physical, mental, cognitive, psychosocial, functional, and environmental needs. Includes structured recording of demographics, problems, medications, and allergies. Supports at least 20 minutes/month of care management per patient.\n\n**Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)**: Captures physiological data from FDA-approved home monitoring devices (glucose monitors, blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, weight scales, heart rate monitors). Data is transmitted in real-time to the care team.\n\n**Medication Therapy Monitoring (MTM) / Drug Adherence**: Tracks medication adherence, provides reminders, monitors for side effects, and checks for drug interactions. Originally developed for oncology medication adherence — this was the company's founding use case.\n\n**Principal Care Management (PCM)**: Extended care management for high-risk patients requiring 30+ minutes of monthly care coordination.\n\n**Care Transitions Management**: Coordination for patients transitioning between settings — includes emergency department follow-up and hospital discharge coordination.\n\n**24/7 Clinical Call Center**: While not a software module per se, this is integral to how the platform operates. Trained clinical staff provide the care management services, logging all interactions in the system.\n\n**AI/ML capabilities**: The vendor claims to use artificial intelligence and machine learning for identifying health risks and enabling preventive interventions, though specific details are not provided.\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on vendor materials, the platform manages the following data:\n\n**Clinical data explicitly described**:\n- Patient demographics\n- Problem lists (chronic conditions)\n- Medication lists and medication allergies\n- Care plans (comprehensive, addressing physical, mental, cognitive, psychosocial, functional, and environmental domains)\n- Physiological monitoring data: glucose, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, weight (from RPM devices)\n- Medication adherence records and side effect reports\n- Clinical summaries\n\n**Interaction and workflow data**:\n- Care coordination logs (documenting the 20+ minutes/month of CCM services)\n- Call center interaction records (200,000+ interactions logged)\n- Secure messages between patients, care teams, and providers\n- Referral and care transition records\n- Patient consent records (required for CCM billing)\n\n**Billing-relevant data**:\n- Time tracking for CCM/PCM/RPM services (linked to CPT codes 99439, 99437, 99487, 99489, 99490, 99491 for CCM; 99424-99427 for PCM)\n- Service documentation supporting Medicare reimbursement\n\n**What's unclear or likely absent**:\n- The website does not describe clinical notes/encounter documentation in the traditional EHR sense (progress notes, H&P, etc.)\n- No mention of lab result storage (though CPOE for labs is certified, suggesting orders can be placed)\n- No mention of diagnostic imaging results\n- No mention of immunization records\n- No mention of scheduling/appointment management\n- No mention of billing/claims processing beyond CCM/PCM/RPM time tracking — the actual Medicare billing appears to be done by the physician practice, not through this system\n- No mention of document management or scanned records\n\nThe product's data footprint is specialized: it's deep on care plans, medication monitoring, physiological data from RPM devices, and care coordination activity logs, but narrow compared to a full EHR. It does not appear to be the primary clinical documentation system for any practice — rather, it supplements the practice's existing EHR with CCM/RPM/MTM-specific capabilities.\n\n---\n","numLines":102,"startLine":1,"totalLines":102}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01QyhoiLY9fv6KAWXTetLLg2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0136oJ2JtyeskjbGJYgPSA4f","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/sargas-pharmaceutical-adherence-and-compliance-international/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Sargas Pharmaceutical Adherence and Compliance International — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://www.spacinternational.com/SPAC-Export.pdf\n- CHPL ID: 10702\n- Product: Sargas International's Chronic Care Management Cloud dba hru2day, VERSION 21.9\n- Certification date: 2021-10-14\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. Probed the registered URL with curl:\n   ```\n   curl -sI -L \"https://www.spacinternational.com/SPAC-Export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, Content-Type: application/pdf, Content-Length: 379759 bytes. Direct PDF download — no redirects.\n\n2. Downloaded the PDF:\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://www.spacinternational.com/SPAC-Export.pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/SPAC-Export.pdf\n   ```\n   Verified with `file` and `pdfinfo`: 1-page PDF, created from \"Microsoft Word - SPAC-Export.docx\", produced with \"Microsoft: Print To PDF\", dated 2023-12-19 (modified 2025-11-25).\n\n3. Extracted full text with `pdftotext`. The PDF contains only 6 sentences describing the export at a very high level.\n\n4. Checked for embedded URLs and attachments — none found.\n\n5. Checked the mandatory disclosures page at https://www.spacinternational.com/certified-ehr-technology.php — it contains only a certification statement paragraph and a link to the mandatory disclosures PDF (ONC-HIT-CERTIFICATE-DISCLOSURE_ver_21_9_Revised-25.pdf). The disclosures PDF lists certified criteria and pricing but no additional EHI export technical detail.\n\n6. Browsed the open `/pdf/` directory at https://www.spacinternational.com/pdf/ — found ~100 PDFs. All are CCM/RPM brochures, consent forms, white papers, billing guides, Real World Testing plans, and enrollment forms. None contain additional EHI export documentation.\n\n7. Probed common alternative paths (/ehi, /ehi-export, /api, /fhir, /interoperability, /data-export) — all returned 404.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a **single 1-page PDF** with 6 sentences. Here is the complete text:\n\n> **Product Name:** Sargas International's Chronic Care Management Cloud dba hru2day®\n>\n> **Product Version:** VERSION 21.9\n>\n> The patient EHI export contains data from the patient's chart. Multiple file formats are used to store this information.\n>\n> ZIP is an archive file format.\n>\n> PDF or Portable Document Format is a file format that is used to present text or image based documents.\n>\n> C-CDA or Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture is a file format used for health information exchange.\n>\n> The export file itself is a zip file. It contains zip files of C-CDAs and PDF files attached to the patient's chart (machine readable PDF)\n>\n> Information for each patient encounter is available C-CDA format in zip archive.\n\nThat is the entirety of the documentation. It tells us:\n- The export is a ZIP file\n- Inside the ZIP are C-CDA documents (one per encounter) and PDF files from the patient's chart\n- The C-CDAs are in nested ZIP archives\n\nThere is no data dictionary, no field-level documentation, no schema, no sample data, no API specification, no user guide for performing the export, and no description of what data fields or sections are included in the C-CDAs.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe documentation says the export \"contains data from the patient's chart\" — but does not specify which data elements are included or excluded. Based on the product research, the hru2day platform stores:\n\n**Likely covered (if C-CDA sections are reasonably populated):**\n- Patient demographics (C-CDA standard section)\n- Problem lists / chronic conditions (C-CDA standard section)\n- Medication lists and allergies (C-CDA standard sections)\n- Clinical summaries (C-CDA standard section)\n\n**Uncertain — no documentation to confirm or deny:**\n- Care plans (the core of what this product does — comprehensive care plans addressing physical, mental, cognitive, psychosocial, functional, and environmental domains). C-CDA has a Care Plan section, but it's unclear if the vendor populates it with the full richness of their care plan data.\n- Physiological monitoring data from RPM devices (glucose, BP, heart rate, SpO2, weight). C-CDA is not well-suited for time-series device data. These may be entirely absent from the export.\n- Medication adherence records and side effect reports. This is the company's founding specialty (Drug Adherence® for oncology patients). C-CDA has no standard section for medication adherence tracking.\n- Care coordination logs (documenting 20+ minutes/month of CCM services) — 200,000+ logged interactions. These are critical billing-supporting records.\n- Call center interaction records\n- Secure messages between patients, care teams, and providers\n- Time tracking for CCM/PCM/RPM services (linked to CPT codes)\n- Patient consent records\n\n**Likely missing:**\n- Billing-relevant time tracking and service documentation. C-CDA is a clinical document standard; it does not accommodate billing/administrative data well.\n- RPM device time-series data. C-CDA cannot reasonably represent continuous glucose readings, daily blood pressure logs, etc.\n- Care coordination activity logs. These are workflow records that are core to the product's purpose but have no C-CDA analog.\n\nThe fundamental concern is that this is a **chronic care management platform** — its primary value is in care plans, care coordination logs, RPM device data, and medication adherence tracking — none of which map cleanly to C-CDA. Using C-CDA as the sole export format for this product likely means the export captures only the clinical summary data (demographics, problems, meds, allergies) while missing the majority of the product's actual data.\n\n### The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Question\n\nThis is not the typical FHIR-as-b(10) confusion, but it's an analogous problem: the vendor appears to be using their **C-CDA clinical summary export** (which would support (e)(2) Clinical Information Reconciliation and general clinical data exchange) as their (b)(10) EHI export. A C-CDA clinical summary is a standardized subset of clinical data — it is not \"all electronic health information\" the product stores. The product's differentiating data (RPM telemetry, care coordination logs, medication adherence tracking, CCM time logs) would require a custom export format, not C-CDA.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: ZIP containing C-CDA XML documents (per encounter) and PDF attachments\n- **Standard**: C-CDA (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture) — a recognized health information exchange standard\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is a reasonable format for clinical summaries but is fundamentally mismatched with the product's core data. A chronic care management platform's most important data — care coordination logs, RPM device readings, medication adherence tracking, time-based billing records — cannot be expressed in C-CDA. A CSV or database dump of care plan tables, RPM readings, and interaction logs would provide far more complete EHI coverage.\n- **Reconstructability**: A third party could reconstruct a basic clinical summary from the C-CDAs, but could not reconstruct the patient's full care management history, device monitoring data, or coordination activity.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **extremely minimal** — arguably the minimum viable compliance artifact. Six sentences on one page:\n- No data dictionary whatsoever\n- No field-level definitions\n- No description of which C-CDA sections are populated\n- No sample data or example files\n- No schema or profile documentation\n- No instructions for how to perform the export (who initiates it, from what screen, what parameters)\n- No description of how PDFs are organized within the ZIP\n- A developer given only this document could not implement an import — they would know only \"it's a ZIP with C-CDAs and PDFs inside.\"\n\nThe documentation reads as a certification checkbox, not a genuine guide to the export.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Product and format level only. No table, field, or section-level detail.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented\n- **Relationships**: Not documented\n- **Versioning**: The PDF was last modified 2025-11-25, originally created 2023-12-19. No change history.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://www.spacinternational.com/SPAC-Export.pdf\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- No obstacles accessing the PDF — it's a direct, unauthenticated download.\n- No additional EHI export documentation found anywhere on the vendor's website despite checking the certification page, mandatory disclosures, the open /pdf/ directory listing (~100 files), and probing common alternative URL paths.\n- The entire vendor website is focused on CCM/RPM service marketing and Medicare billing compliance. Technical product documentation appears to be essentially absent from the public-facing site.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":319,"cache_read_input_tokens":55498,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":319},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"75646119-9221-4382-b7e5-5d3f8f25469b","uuid":"473c2897-a9e6-46a8-96cd-7918d42e5230"}
